meta.title: Whose vision of Jesus is better — rationally and historically?
meta.thesis: Comparing the Christian vision (incarnate Son, crucified and risen Lord) with the Islamic vision (exalted human Messiah-prophet), which is more coherent rationally and better grounded historically?
meta.purpose: Integrate identity, history, and worship: not only 'did he die?' but 'what must Jesus be for the story to make sense?' Steelman both portraits as live religious options.
meta.warning: This overlaps Trinity, historical Jesus, and morality dossiers. Lead with the vision (who Jesus is and why it matters), then pull receipts. Don't get lost in only 4:157.

definitions.precise: Eternal Son incarnate, truly God and truly man, crucified for sins, risen, worthy of worship, returning as judge — with denominational nuances.
definitions.not: Not every modern liberal Protestant minimization.

definitions.precise: Virgin-born Messiah, prophet, word from God, worker of signs by permission, not divine, not crucified (per majority reading), returning before the Hour in many traditions.
definitions.not: Not a denial that Jesus matters — Islam gives him high honor without deity.

definitions.precise: Internal consistency of the portrait with monotheism, justice, and Jesus' own role.
Fit with earliest recoverable data about Jesus and his movement.
definitions.not: Not popularity or later empire success.

definitions.precise: Whether Jesus is a proper recipient of latria/devotion due to God alone.
definitions.not: Not whether Jesus is respected as prophet.

definitions.precise: Christian strategies for incarnation coherence (self-emptying; Chalcedonian natures).
definitions.not: Not required vocabulary for Muslims — but Christians must be ready to explain.

arguments.title: Which portrait fits earliest data better?

christian.claim: Earliest sources show a crucified Messiah proclaimed risen and worshipped — the Christian vision is the organic development of that data; the Islamic vision truncates it.
christian.case: 1 Cor 15; Phil 2; Synoptic passion. A prophet who didn't die under Pilate fails the first historical filter.

data_points.fact: Cross + early devotion + 1 Cor 15 appearances are the Christian portrait's historical spine.
data_points.label: Cross + early devotion + 1 Cor 15 appearances are the Christian portrait's historical spine.

muslim.claim: Earliest recoverable Jesus is a Jewish monotheist prophet — the Islamic vision preserves that core while Christian vision inflates post-Easter metaphysics.
muslim.case: Shema affirmation; prophet-in-Israel paradigm; critical dating of high Johannine discourse.

data_points.fact: Jewish monotheism + prophet-within-Israel is the Islamic portrait's historical spine; incarnation is the extra.
data_points.label: Jewish monotheism + prophet-within-Israel is the Islamic portrait's historical spine; incarnation is the extra.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Organic development can still be wrong development.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: If you grant critical tools, crucifixion usually comes with the 'prophet' core.
arguments.crux: Is the passion-kerygma historical bedrock or theological overwrite?
arguments.debate_use: Start with a 60-second 'earliest data' dump both must answer.
arguments.why_it_matters: This topic's engine: not 'which religion is nicer,' but which Jesus-picture is better motivated by early data plus reason.

live.if_they_say: Our Jesus is obviously the real one.
live.you_say: Split the scorecard: (1) 1st-century sources, (2) Jewish monotheism, (3) moral meaning, (4) worship practice. Don't let one category bully the rest.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't call the other portrait 'a different Jesus' as a slur until you show contradiction, not just emphasis.

arguments.title: Fit with monotheism

christian.claim: Incarnational monotheism (one essence) rationally allows Jesus' worship without second god; the vision solves how God reveals Himself personally.
christian.case: John 1; Hebrews 1. Trinity dossier applies; here stress Jesus as God's self-word.

quotes.text: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one… and one Lord, Jesus Christ…

muslim.claim: The Islamic vision is the clean monotheistic portrait: exalted servant, never God. Christian vision multiplies rational burdens (Trinity + incarnation).
muslim.case: 112; 4:171; 5:75. Occam + tawhid: honor Jesus without ontological confusion.

quotes.text: They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary.'

arguments.counter_to_christian: Identity theories of incarnation remain philosophically costly.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Cleanliness that underfits historical worship data may be false economy.
arguments.crux: Prefer simpler monotheism or data-fitting incarnational monotheism?
arguments.debate_use: Score 'simplicity' and 'data fit' as separate numbers.
arguments.why_it_matters: Same fork as Trinity topic; here it is applied to Jesus' identity rather than abstract God.

live.you_say: If Jesus is the incarnate Word of the one God, it is not a second god. If he is only a prophet, it is shirk. The identity claim is the whole debate — don't smuggle the conclusion into the definition.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't pretend the grammar is intuitive to a 7th-century Arabian polemic. Don't pretend 5:17 doesn't exist.

arguments.title: Moral meaning of the cross vs denial

christian.claim: A crucified God-with-us uniquely discloses divine love and justice; denying the cross removes the Christian vision's moral center.
christian.case: Romans 5:8; 1 Cor 1:18–25. The scandal is the point — wisdom through apparent weakness.

quotes.text: But God proves his love for us in that while we still were sinners Christ died for us.

muslim.claim: God's rescue of His prophet (4:157–158) better fits divine justice than orchestrating the killing of His son; mercy does not need blood.
muslim.case: 39:53; 4:157. Vicarious punishment is the rational scandal Muslims refuse.

quotes.text: No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.

data_points.fact: Islam: God forgives by tawba and mercy without a blood payment; a crucified God looks unnecessary or unjust.
data_points.label: Islam: God forgives by tawba and mercy without a blood payment; a crucified God looks unnecessary or unjust.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Love could be shown without penal mechanisms — argue necessity.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: If the movement's center was cross-proclamation, rescue-without-death must explain Christian origins.
arguments.crux: Is the cross a moral necessity of love/justice or a moral impossibility for God?
arguments.why_it_matters: Even if 4:157 can be reread, the cross as saving event is still the Christian vision's heart.

live.you_say: If the Son freely offers himself and is one with the Father, it is not a third-party child. If you reject that identity, the moral objection follows. Identity again.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't mock Jewish/Christian sacrifice language. Don't pretend 6:164 was written as a commentary on Anselm.

arguments.title: Shared high titles: word, spirit, messiah

christian.claim: Qur'anic high titles for Jesus (word, spirit) unstablely sit beside denial of deity; Christian vision integrates those honors coherently in Logos Christology.
christian.case: 4:171 names; John 1 integrates. Muslims must explain why 'word' isn't personal Logos.

quotes.text: The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was a messenger of Allah and His word… and a spirit from Him.
quotes.work: Muslim-usable and Christian-usable in different ways

muslim.claim: Titles are honorific/creational agency, not ontology; Christian integration over-reads Semitic speech into Greek hypostases.
muslim.case: 3:45; 4:171. 'Word cast to Mary' = creative kun command, not second person of Trinity.

data_points.fact: Kalimah and rūḥ are honors that still sit under 'do not say Three.'
data_points.label: Kalimah and rūḥ are honors that still sit under 'do not say Three.'

arguments.counter_to_christian: Lexical overlap ≠ conceptual identity across languages/centuries.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: If titles are so high, the worship boundary needs clear principled line.
arguments.crux: Do shared titles favor Christian integration or Islamic non-ontological honor?
arguments.debate_use: Ban the word 'clearly' for this argument — only parse.
arguments.why_it_matters: Shared high titles are a trap: each side thinks the other is inches from converting.

live.if_they_say: The Qur'an already calls Jesus the Word, so he is God.
live.you_say: Read the rest of 4:171: messenger, do not say Three, Allah is one God. Title-sharing is not hypostatic union.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't strip 4:171 of its tawhid ending. Don't strip it of 'word' and 'spirit' either.

arguments.title: Virgin birth: shared sign, divergent meaning

christian.claim: Virgin birth signals unique Sonship and new-creation Adam typology; Islam keeps the sign while rejecting the meaning Christians take it to carry.
christian.case: Luke 1; Matt 1. Shared supernatural origin increases pressure on 'mere prophet' minimalism.

quotes.text: The angel said to her, 'The Holy Spirit will come upon you… therefore the child to be born will be holy; he will be called Son of God.'

muslim.claim: 3:59 — Jesus like Adam: created by command; virgin birth shows God's power, not deity of the child.
muslim.case: Adam had no parents; Jesus' miraculous birth is not a Trinity argument.

quotes.text: The likeness of Jesus with Allah is as the likeness of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was.
quotes.work: Virgin birth as creation sign, not deity

arguments.counter_to_christian: Adam typology can cut Islamic direction too.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Christians don't argue virgin birth alone proves deity — it coheres in a larger pattern.
arguments.crux: Is virgin birth a sign of unique incarnation or of creative power only?
arguments.debate_use: Treat as supporting argument, not the main hinge.
arguments.why_it_matters: Rare agreement. Use it as a control: shared miracle, divergent meaning.

live.if_they_say: Virgin birth proves Jesus is the Son of God.
live.you_say: Luke connects it to 'Son of God.' The Qur'an connects it to Adam. Same sign, two interpretations — don't treat the miracle as a unique Christian possession.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't deny the Muslim virgin birth. Don't pretend 3:59 is Johannine Logos.

arguments.title: Return of Jesus in both visions

christian.claim: Jesus' return as judge fits the Christian vision of cosmic Lordship; Islamic second-coming traditions implicitly concede extraordinary eschatological status.
christian.case: Acts 1:11; Matt 25. Muslim hadith eschatology of Jesus' return is a pressure point on 'only prophet' rhetoric.

quotes.text: This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven.

muslim.claim: Jesus' return (in hadith-based eschatology) is as a follower of Muhammad's sharīʿa, breaking the cross — confirming Islam's vision, not Nicene Lordship.
muslim.case: Popular Muslim eschatology: Jesus denies Christian exaggeration. Qur'anic base is thinner; be honest about hadith weight.

sources.label: Sahih Muslim 2897 (Jesus return themes — check numbering/collections)

data_points.fact: Hadith: Jesus returns, breaks the cross, kills the swine, abolishes jizya — a distinctly Islamic future Jesus.
data_points.source: Sahih Bukhari 2476 / Muslim 155 (standard citations in this debate)
data_points.label: Hadith: Jesus returns, breaks the cross, kills the swine, abolishes jizya — a distinctly Islamic future Jesus.
data_points.note: Sahih Bukhari 2476 / Muslim 155 (standard citations in this debate)

arguments.counter_to_christian: Hadith eschatology isn't Nicene Christology; don't over-claim.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Why does history culminate with Jesus' return if Muhammad is the seal in all senses?
arguments.crux: Does eschatological Jesus support Christian cosmic Lordship or Islamic finality of Muhammad?
arguments.why_it_matters: Eschatology overlap that still splits: Jesus returns as judge-Messiah vs as Muslim who breaks the cross.

live.if_they_say: We both believe Jesus is coming back, so we're close.
live.you_say: Close on the return, far on who he is when he returns. Ask whether he comes to be worshiped or to correct those who worshiped him.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't treat all second-coming hadith as Qur'an. Don't treat Acts 1 as Qur'an either.

arguments.title: Do you pray to Jesus?

christian.claim: New Testament pattern includes prayer/invocation directed to Jesus; the vision requires worship. If Jesus is only a prophet, Christian liturgy is idolatry — the stakes are real.
christian.case: Acts 7:59; 1 Cor 1:2; Rev 5. Rationally: either Christians are deeply wrong or Muslims under-rank Jesus.

quotes.text: Stephen prayed, 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.'

muslim.claim: Prayer to Jesus is the error the Qur'an corrects; true followers of Jesus prayed to the Father alone.
muslim.case: 5:116–117; John 17:3 as unitarian proof-text. Islamic vision protects worship.

quotes.text: Indeed, those who say, 'Our Lord is Allah,' and then remain steadfast — the angels descend upon them…
quotes.work: Worship directed to Allah alone as the safe pattern

arguments.counter_to_christian: Later liturgical development ≠ Jesus' own teaching on prayer (Lord's Prayer to Father).
arguments.counter_to_muslim: If earliest Christians invoked Jesus, Islamic correction must indict apostolic practice, not only councils.
arguments.crux: Is invoking Jesus required fidelity or defining idolatry?
arguments.debate_use: Ask both speakers to answer yes/no: may a Christian say 'Lord Jesus, have mercy'?
arguments.why_it_matters: The practice test from the Trinity topic, aimed at Jesus personally.

live.if_they_say: We only pray through Jesus, not to Jesus.
live.you_say: Acts 7:59 looks like prayer to Jesus. Many liturgies address the Son directly. If that's still not 'to,' define worship so the audience can test it.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't ignore 'through Christ' language. Don't let it hide the addressee.

arguments.title: Jesus' role in salvation

christian.claim: Jesus is not only teacher but Savior; the vision stands or falls on unique mediation (John 14:6; Acts 4:12).
christian.case: Without unique saving death/resurrection, Jesus becomes one prophet among many — a different religion.

quotes.text: There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.

muslim.claim: Jesus saves as prophet by guiding to tawhid; God alone forgives. Unique mediation of a God-man is unnecessary and unjust.
muslim.case: 3:51; 19:36; 39:53. The Islamic vision keeps Savior-language for God.

quotes.text: Say, 'If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins.'
quotes.work: Forgiveness via following the Prophet, not via Calvary

arguments.counter_to_christian: Exclusivism must face the sincere-outsider problem.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Guidance-only Jesus undercuts the urgency and content of apostolic preaching.
arguments.crux: Is Jesus Savior in a unique mediatorial sense, or messenger of the Savior-God?
arguments.debate_use: Force a one-sentence soteriology from each side.
arguments.why_it_matters: Soteriology is why the portraits cannot be merged by goodwill.

live.if_they_say: Jesus is just a prophet in both religions.
live.you_say: Not in Christianity: he is savior. In Islam he is messenger and messiah without atonement. 'Just a prophet' is already picking Islam's portrait.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't erase Islamic honor of Jesus. Don't shrink Christian claims to 'great teacher.'

arguments.title: What was the Injīl?

christian.claim: If Injīl means the Gospel about Jesus' death and resurrection, Islam's affirmation of Injīl collides with its Christology; if not, 'Gospel' is equivocal.
christian.case: Islamic dilemma adjacent: 5:46–47. Christian vision claims continuity with apostolic gospel.

data_points.fact: 4th-c. complete-ish Greek Bibles predate Islam; crucifixion and high Christology are already in them.
data_points.label: 4th-c. complete-ish Greek Bibles predate Islam; crucifixion and high Christology are already in them.

muslim.claim: Injīl is revelation given to Jesus, not identical to four canonical biographies with Pauline theology; Christian vision confuses later texts with Jesus' Gospel.
muslim.case: 5:46; tahrif debates. Rational: judge Jesus by Jesus' message, not church canon alone.

quotes.text: Since the 'authorized' scriptures of Jews and Christians remain very much today as they existed at the time of the Prophet, it is difficult to argue that the Qur'anic references to Tawrat and Injil were only to the 'pure' Tawrat and Injil as existed at the time of Moses and Jesus.
quotes.work: The Charge of Distortion of Jewish and Christian Scriptures

data_points.fact: Muslim reply still: Injil is a revelation to Jesus, not a later four-fold canon; tahrif can be of meaning.
data_points.label: Muslim reply still: Injil is a revelation to Jesus, not a later four-fold canon; tahrif can be of meaning.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Equating Injīl with the fourfold canon begs the question.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: A free-floating Injīl without recoverable content is hard to follow historically.
arguments.crux: What publicly recoverable content counts as Jesus' Gospel?
arguments.debate_use: Define Injīl before any dilemma or corruption argument.
arguments.why_it_matters: If Injil ≠ four Gospels, the Islamic Jesus can float free of Mark. If it ≈ the Gospel Christians had in 632, collision returns.

live.if_they_say: Show me the Injil of Jesus.
live.you_say: If you mean a lost single book, neither of us can table it. If you mean what Christians were reading in the 7th century, we can: it already had a crucified, worshiped Jesus.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't invent a reconstructed Injil. Don't pretend 5:47 doesn't exist.

arguments.title: Finality: Jesus vs Muhammad as hermeneutical key

christian.claim: If Jesus is God's final and personal revelation (Heb 1:1–3), later contradictory claims about him are rationally secondary.
christian.case: Christians argue the best vision of Jesus cannot be adjudicated by a later prophet who denies the passion center.

quotes.text: And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, to be with you forever. This is the Spirit of truth…
quotes.work: Paraclete as Spirit, not a later Arabian prophet (Christian reading)

muslim.claim: God's final revelation (Qur'an) clarifies disputes among People of the Book; rational humility accepts correction of earlier communities' excess about Jesus.
muslim.case: 5:48; 4:171. Seal of prophets frame (33:40) includes correcting Christology.

quotes.text: And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, 'O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you… giving good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad.'

arguments.counter_to_christian: Hebrews' finality is itself a faith claim inside the Christian canon.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Finality claims can't skip historical confrontation with 1st-c. sources.
arguments.crux: Who has standing to give the definitive vision of Jesus — apostolic witnesses or the Qur'an?
arguments.debate_use: This is often the real meta-debate — surface it early.
arguments.why_it_matters: Ahmad/Paraclete fights try to make Jesus a pointer to Muhammad.

live.you_say: Q 61:6 is the Islamic claim. John 14's paraklētos is the Spirit in Christian reading. Don't bounce Greek periklytos memes without a manuscript. Fight the identity of the promised one with texts on the table.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't claim a Greek manuscript of periklytos unless you can show it. Don't claim 61:6 is quoting John.

arguments.title: Full humanity without docetism

christian.claim: Chalcedonian vision insists on full humanity (hunger, grief, death) against docetism; some Islamic substitution readings risk appearing docetic about the cross event.
christian.case: Hebrews 2:14–18; John 11:35. Real incarnation requires real death for real solidarity.

muslim.claim: Qur'an stresses Jesus' full creaturely humanity (eats food) precisely against deification; denying crucifixion is not docetism about his life but about his enemies' victory.
muslim.case: 5:75; 19:30–33. Islamic vision blocks both Arian and Nicene errors by different means.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Two-natures itself risks conceptual docetism if divinity swallows humanity.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Substitution theories historically often look docetic about the one on the cross.
arguments.crux: Which vision better secures that the real Jesus suffered history's violence?
arguments.debate_use: Ask: who suffered on the cross, if anyone?
arguments.why_it_matters: Docetism accusation: if Jesus only seemed to die, his humanity is at risk both in some tafsīr and in some Christian heresies.

live.if_they_say: Islam honors Jesus' humanity more because he is only a man.
live.you_say: A prophet who does not truly die can become less human, not more — that's the docetism warning. Chalcedon insists he is fully human. Score the claim against substitution tafsīr and against Apollinarianism, not against a slogan.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't say all Muslims are docetists. Don't say all Christians have a credible Jesus of Nazareth.

arguments.title: Existential / transformative adequacy

christian.claim: The Christian vision offers personal union with God in Christ and liberation from guilt via the cross — existentially thicker than prophet-veneration alone.
christian.case: Galatians 2:20; Romans 8. Rational evaluation of a vision includes what it does in moral psychology.

muslim.claim: Islamic vision yields ʿubūdiyya without idolatry anxiety: love and follow Jesus while worshipping God alone — spiritually safer and clearer.
muslim.case: 3:51; 112. Transformation via tawba, ṣalāh, and following prophets without confusing Creator/creature.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Existential thickness can be psychologically powerful and still false.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Clarity can be existentially thin if it misses the movement's cross-shaped core.
arguments.crux: Should existential adequacy count heavily, or only as a tiebreaker after history/logic?
arguments.debate_use: Weight this argument last; don't let testimony replace history.
arguments.why_it_matters: Existential tie-breaker audiences feel: which portrait actually changes people?

live.if_they_say: Our Jesus changes lives, so he is the real one.
live.you_say: Transformation is data about communities, not a manuscript. Saints and sinners exist in both. Use it as a closing illustration after history and coherence, not as a proof that skips 4:157 or John 1.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't weaponize anecdotes. Don't sneer at the other community's piety.

live.if_they_say: Ally already showed the Christian Jesus is later theology.
live.you_say: Steal the method-symmetry demand. Then put 1 Cor 8:6 and 1 Cor 15 next to Q 4:171. A debate clip is not a stemma.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't treat Ally as Ehrman. Don't treat White as Hurtado.

materials.title: Papyrus 𝔓52 (Rylands) — John 18
materials.significance: Tiny fragment of John 18; among the earliest surviving NT witnesses. Proves a Johannine text was circulating in Egypt within ~100 years of composition — not photographic proof of events, but strong early textuality evidence.
materials.debate_use: Use against 'Gospels invented in 4th century.' Do not overclaim 'proves inerrancy.'

materials.title: Codex Sinaiticus (א)
materials.significance: Nearly complete Greek Bible including NT. Landmark for reconstructing the early text; also contains famous readings (e.g. ending of Mark issues) that honest Christian apologetics must own.
materials.debate_use: Open the digital leaf live if possible. Transparency > slogan.

materials.title: Dead Sea Scrolls — Great Isaiah Scroll
materials.significance: Pushes Hebrew Bible textual history back centuries before Islam. Shows substantial continuity with later MT and also real plurality (MT/LXX-like types). Context for Jesus' Judaism.
materials.debate_use: Destroys 'OT invented in Middle Ages.' Does not prove zero variation.

materials.title: Birmingham Qur'an folios (Mingana 1572a)
materials.significance: High-profile early Qur'anic leaves. Media overclaimed 'oldest Qur'an'; academically: dates parchment, not ink; text is early Uthmanic-type. Strong proximity evidence.
materials.debate_use: Affirm impressiveness; force C-14 literacy (parchment vs writing event).

materials.title: Ṣanʿāʾ palimpsest (DAM 01-27.1 / C-1)
materials.significance: Only substantial manuscript witness to a non-Uthmanic Qur'anic text-type. Word/phrase variants; Sadeghi stemmatics argue Uthmanic closer to prototype. Challenges folk clone-identity; supports early multiplicity.
materials.debate_use: Both sides can use it — know BOTH uses before the round.

materials.title: Papyrus 𝔓46 — Pauline letters
materials.significance: Early collection of Paul. Relevant to historicity because Paul's letters (50s) are earliest Christian literature and already contain high Christology + crucifixion kerygma.
materials.debate_use: Bridge from manuscripts to content: early text + early theology of the cross.

debates.title: Nature / identity of Jesus debates
debates.summary: Standard pattern: Synoptic unitarian readings vs early worship + John + creed; crucifixion returns as historical veto.
what_to_steal: Ask what would falsify each vision

opponent_cards.trigger: We Muslims love Jesus more — we mention him respectfully
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Honor is real in the Qur'an. The dispute is identity and cross, not courtesy titles.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask whether praying to Jesus is shirk by definition.

opponent_cards.fast_answer: On Christian vision, they worship God the Son incarnate — not a mere man. State the ontology.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Then fight whether that ontology is true.

opponent_cards.fast_answer: That's an Islamic claim about Injīl content. Historically, recover it in 1st-c. sources or concede it's revelation-only.

opponent_cards.trigger: The Bible is corrupted so only the Qur'an shows the real Jesus
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Specify what kind of tahrif. For history, we still have 1st-c. sources to weigh.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask which recoverable Jesus-teachings they accept.

opponent_cards.trigger: Trinity was invented; Jesus was unitarian
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Distinguish development of terms from eruption of Jesus-devotion. Use historical Jesus dossier tools.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Mark 12:29 AND Phil 2 both on the table.

opponent_cards.trigger: God would never let His prophet be crucified
opponent_cards.fast_answer: That's a theological intuition. Christian vision: He did, for redemption. Argue justice, don't only intuit.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask how they explain the historical consensus.

opponent_cards.fast_answer: Powerful unitarian-sounding text; Christians read it with John 1 and 20:28. Don't isolate.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask how Thomas's confession is classified.

opponent_cards.trigger: Jesus ate food so he can't be God
opponent_cards.fast_answer: That's anti-Docetism / full humanity — Christians agree he ate. Chalcedon: humanity isn't a veto on deity.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask if any incarnation theory could satisfy them in principle.

opponent_cards.trigger: Your Gospels contradict, so your Jesus vision is incoherent
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Harmonistics vs contradiction claims are a sub-debate. Vision coherence ≠ synopsis of every chronology.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Offer core kerygma shared across sources.

opponent_cards.trigger: Islam's Jesus is just a way to deny Christianity
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Steelman: Islam places Jesus in a line of prophets with honor. Then critique collisions.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Affirm virgin birth/miracles overlap before fighting cross/deity.

opponent_cards.trigger: If Jesus is God, who ran the universe when he died?
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Classical answer: divine nature didn't cease; death is in the human nature. Explain without mockery.
Mystery ≠ contradiction. Demand a formal contradiction; cite SEP incarnation models.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Compare burdens: incarnation vs 4:157 vs history.

Announce weights: history vs rationality vs existential

Prepare cross necessity vs cross impossibility exchange
Link to trinity and historical_jesus dossiers without dumping whole files
Falsification: what would make you abandon your vision?
Drill cards; steelman Islamic honor of Jesus first
Separate Qur'an-only from hadith eschatology on return
Closing: data fit + monotheism coherence, not slogans
Bring Chalcedon line + Q 4:171 + 1 Cor 15 card

Christian podium: Vision integrates earliest cross/resurrection kerygma and Jesus-devotion
Incarnational monotheism explains worship without crude tritheism
Cross as disclosure of love/justice is existentially and theologically central
Islamic vision underfits passion history and apostolic gospel content
Muslim podium: Vision preserves uncompromising tawhid while highly honoring Jesus
Prophet-Messiah portrait better matches Jewish monotheist historical core
Rejects moral scandal of vicarious divine death; mercy without blood
Unity / steelman: Both visions treat Jesus as pivotal — not peripheral
Agree on virgin birth and miracles-by-God's-power as shared affirmations to isolate forks
Distinguish respect, worship, and historical reconstruction
Name the meta-authority: apostolic witnesses vs Qur'an
